subject: Aligning a short 30-min product intro + stakeholder shortlist
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.w@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@helixcloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aligning a short 30-min product intro + stakeholder shortlist

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery: HelixCloud is evaluating inference options for customer-facing generative features where low median latency and predictable cost are priorities, and you flagged model governance and auditability as hard constraints.

Proposed next step: a focused 30-minute product intro that covers live demo, hosting options (hosted vs. dedicated), and our audit/retention primitives so your security lead gets what they need. To make this useful, could you confirm which of the people below should attend? If there are others we should include, please add.

Suggested attendee shortlist (you can edit):
- Miguel Alvarez — Head of ML (tech owner)
- Priya Shah — Platform Security (security/compliance)
- Samira Khan — Director, Product (decision owner)

Available 30-minute windows (PDT):
- Option A: Tue Apr 2, 10:00–10:30
- Option B: Wed Apr 3, 14:00–14:30
- Option C: Thu Apr 4, 08:30–09:00

If Priya prefers a brief 15-minute pre-call specifically for SOC2/retention questions, we can schedule that immediately before the demo. I’ve attached a short post-call deck and a worksheet that helps us scope the workload and infra needs.

Please pick your preferred slot and confirm attendees; I’ll send the calendar invite and a short mutual action plan (one-pager) after you confirm. Calendly link if easier: https://calendly.com/logan/30min

Best,
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.w@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0187
Redwood Inference — Make inference predictable

Attachments: 2029-04-01_postcall-deck.pdf, helix_requirements.xlsx
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@helixcloud.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.w@redwood.ai>
Cc: Miguel Alvarez <miguel.alvarez@helixcloud.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@helixcloud.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2029 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning a short 30-min product intro + stakeholder shortlist

Hi Logan —

Thanks for the clear recap. Wed Apr 3, 14:00–14:30 (Option B) works best for our group. Attendees I expect to join:
- Samira Khan (me) — Product
- Miguel Alvarez — Head of ML
- Priya Shah — Platform Security (will attend the demo)

A couple quick asks before the demo:
1) Can you share a one-page SOC2 summary or the specific controls you expose that relate to data retention and audit logs? Priya will want to validate what evidence we can obtain and whether logs meet our retention policy.
2) Any short notes on recommended model quantization/latency tradeoffs for 8k context chat workloads — Miguel’s curious.

If Priya would rather have a 15-minute pre-call focused purely on compliance, she said she could do Apr 3 at 13:30. Otherwise, we’ll catch her in the 14:00 slot.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the calendar invite.
Samira
Samira Khan
Director, Product — HelixCloud
samira.k@helixcloud.com | +1 617-555-2244

Logan / Jordan —

Heads up on a few prep items from Samira’s reply:
- Priya will likely press on SOC2 evidence and retention windows; pull the SOC2-summary.pdf and a short list of where logs are surfaced in the console.
- Miguel will want latency/quantization tradeoffs; plan to show a slide with measured p50/p95 on the 8k chat benchmark (include batch sizes).
- Bring a one-slide mutual action plan with success criteria and next steps (POC scale, KPIs, timeline).

From: Logan Wright <logan.w@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 03 Apr 2029 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning a short 30-min product intro + stakeholder shortlist

Thanks Samira — calendar invite sent for Wed Apr 3, 14:00–14:30 PDT (invitation includes a 15-minute pre-call at 13:30 for Priya; Priya you can ignore the pre-call invite if you prefer).

In advance of the meeting I attached a short SOC2 summary and a draft mutual action plan (MAP) that outlines the POC scope and key milestones. Quick links:
- MAP (read-only): https://drive.redwood.ai/hlx/MAP-HLX-2029-007
- SOC2 summary (attached): SOC2-summary.pdf

Short answers for Miguel: we’ll demo two quantization profiles — 4-bit int8/quant and a float16 path — and show p50/p95 measurements for 256 and 2048 token contexts. We’ll also highlight the autoscaling behavior for burst traffic and what to expect for cost per 1k tokens at different batch sizes.

If there’s anything else to add to the agenda, flag it here and I’ll slot it in. Looking forward to the discussion.

Best,
Logan
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf
